correctness.rationale: Reduction modulo (t) rules out valuation zero. If 2j>=n then the product vanishes by degree, giving q^(n-1) high-valuation elements including zero and the stated counts by leading nonzero coefficient. At 2j<n the leading coefficient is c_j tau^j(c_j), nonzero in the field-coefficient case. In the split case write x=t^j(A+B s) with s^2=1 and sF(t)=F(-t)s. Moving the second t^j to the left multiplies the first s-part by (-1)^j, giving the two listed congruences modulo t^(n-2j). At even j their constant terms force both A_0 and B_0 to vanish. At odd j, A_0=±B_0≠0, and divisibility by the unit B reduces the second equation to A(t)=A(-t) modulo that power. Each of the two possible constants gives exactly one even root of B(t)B(-t) there, by recursion with invertible 2A_0. There are (q-1)q^(n-j-1) choices of B and q^j independent lifts of each root. The number of odd j at most (n-1)/2 is floor((n+1)/4), giving the claimed exact totals and unbounded ratio. Independently, for s^2=d with d nonzero and sigma(F)=F(-t), the commutator of A+B s and C+D s has scalar part d(B sigma(D)-D sigma(B)) and s-part (A-sigma(A))D-(C-sigma(C))B, all modulo t^n. Thus the coordinate map changing d=1 to a nonsquare preserves the entire commutation predicate and all corresponding centralizer sets and dimensions, not their algebra structures. For p=n the Cayley parameter t=(r-1)/(r+1) of k[C_p] is defined because r+1 has augmentation two; t^p=0, sts=-t and the inverse formula recovers r. The surjection between equal-dimensional algebras verifies the dihedral specialization. The finite Ore checker and recorded raw output were inspected, not rerun; extension fields and arbitrary lengths are established by the algebraic proof.

value.rationale: What is useful here is not merely that some rings with identical commuting graphs can have different squaring statistics. This explicit same-field linear equivalence has an unbounded disparity at fixed q, with a complete structural explanation by filtration and parity, and a natural modular dihedral specialization. The exact layer law can be used to compare multiplication invariants that the prior pairwise commutation invariant overlooks.
